# pcd_compute_instance_change_tenant (Action)

Moves an instance to another project, with its ports and attached volumes: the PCD UI's **Change Tenant**. The instance keeps its ID, addresses and owner. Nova checks everything before it moves anything and refuses with its reason, for example an instance with a floating IP, one in a server group, a security group the target project does not own, or a volume with snapshots; the action then fails with Nova's message. After Nova answers, the action reads the instance until it reports the new project.

Needs an admin token, and a PCD release whose Nova has the `changeTenant` action (PCD 2026.8 has it). Afterwards only an admin token can read the instance from a configuration scoped to the old project, so a configuration that manages the instance hands it over to the target project's configuration: see "Moving an instance to another project" in the importing guide. The instance must be active, shut off, paused or suspended, with no task in progress, and not locked.

~> **Requires Terraform 1.14 or later.** Actions are a Terraform 1.14 feature. Resources and data sources are
expected to keep working on older versions, but a configuration that declares an `action` block or an
`action_trigger` does not load.

An action runs only when it is invoked and stores nothing in state. Invoke it from a resource's
`lifecycle` `action_trigger` (on `after_create` or `after_update`), or once from the command line:

```shell
terraform apply -invoke=action.pcd_compute_instance_change_tenant.<name>
```

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.14"
}

data "pcd_identity_project" "team_b" {
  name = "team-b"
}

# Nova moves an instance only when the target project can use its network,
# image and flavor, and owns every security group on its ports (security
# groups do not move). So this example assumes a public image and flavor, and
# puts the instance on a shared network through a port with no security groups.
resource "pcd_networking_network" "example" {
  name   = "tf-example-network"
  shared = true
}

resource "pcd_networking_subnet" "example" {
  network_id = pcd_networking_network.example.id
  cidr       = "10.0.0.0/24"
}

resource "pcd_networking_port" "web" {
  network_id         = pcd_networking_network.example.id
  security_group_ids = []

  depends_on = [pcd_networking_subnet.example]
}

resource "pcd_compute_instance" "web" {
  name        = "tf-example-web"
  image_name  = "Ubuntu-22.04"
  flavor_name = "m1.small"

  network {
    port = pcd_networking_port.web.id
  }
}

# The PCD UI's Change Tenant: moves the instance, its ports and its attached
# volumes to team-b. Needs an admin token. Run it once:
#   terraform apply -invoke=action.pcd_compute_instance_change_tenant.web
# then hand the instance over to team-b's configuration (see "Moving an
# instance to another project" in the importing guide).
action "pcd_compute_instance_change_tenant" "web" {
  config {
    instance_id = pcd_compute_instance.web.id
    project_id  = data.pcd_identity_project.team_b.id
  }
}

# Several instances: one action instance per VM. Set the variable and run one
# on its own with:
#   terraform apply -var 'move_to_team_b=["<instance id>"]' \
#     -invoke='action.pcd_compute_instance_change_tenant.batch["<instance id>"]'
variable "move_to_team_b" {
  description = "IDs of the instances to move to team-b."
  type        = set(string)
  default     = []
}

action "pcd_compute_instance_change_tenant" "batch" {
  for_each = var.move_to_team_b

  config {
    instance_id = each.value
    project_id  = data.pcd_identity_project.team_b.id
  }
}
```

<!-- action schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The ID of the instance to move.
- `project_id` (String) The ID of the project to move the instance to. When the instance is already there, the action moves nothing and warns.

### Optional

- `region` (String) The region the instance is in. Defaults to the provider's region.
